_notes: Speaking prompts consolidated and de-duplicated from teaching notes across multiple students. Part 1/3 questions and Part 2 cue cards are short, formulaic IELTS-style prompts reused as-is (same reasoning as writing-bank.json).

questions: Where is your hometown?
What do you like about your hometown?
What do you not like about it?
How important is your hometown to you?
Do you think you will continue to live in your hometown?
What's the difference between your hometown and other cities in your country?
Would you recommend your hometown to a foreign visitor?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Tell me about the kind of accommodation you live in.
Does the place you live in have many amenities?
Is there anything you would like to change about the place you live in?
Do you plan to live there for a long time?
How long have you lived in your current home?
What's your favourite room in your home?
Do you live with family or by yourself?
Do you have a job right now, or are you a student?
What kind of jobs do people usually do in your country?
What was your first job?
Would you like to change your job in the future?
What do you like or dislike about your job?
What subject are you studying, or what field do you work in?
Is your job or your study stressful?
What do you hope to be doing in five years' time?
Do you enjoy shopping? Why or why not?
How often do you go shopping?
Do you prefer shopping alone or with friends? Why?
Do you plan ahead before you go shopping, or do you buy things on impulse?
What kind of shops do you like visiting?
Do you enjoy shopping online?
Has the way you shop changed in recent years?
Do you often eat with friends?
What kind of food do you usually eat with your friends?
Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants with friends?
Has your taste in food changed since you were a child?
Do you enjoy cooking?
What's your favourite meal of the day?
Do you think it's important to eat healthily?
What do you do in your free time?
Do you have a busy social life?
Do you lead an active life?
Would you like to change anything about your lifestyle?
How much free time do you have during the week?
What did you enjoy doing in your free time as a child?
Do you prefer relaxing at home or going out?
What types of sports are popular in your country?
In your opinion, what are the benefits of playing a sport?
Do you think old people can keep fit by playing sports or exercising?
Do you think famous sports stars make good role models for children?
Do you play any sports yourself?
Did you do much sport when you were a child?
Is it easy to do sports where you live?
How often do you read?
Do you like reading books? Why?
Do you have many books at home?
Do you prefer to buy books or borrow them?
What are the major benefits of reading?
What was the last book you read?
Did your parents encourage you to read as a child?
Do you read in paper form or on a screen?
Do you like watching films?
What kinds of movies do you like best?
Do you like to watch movies alone or with your friends?
Would you like to be in a movie?
How often do you go to the cinema?
Do you prefer local films or foreign films?
What was the last film you watched?
Do you use any apps or technology for cooking or ordering food?
How do you usually plan your meals?
Do you think technology makes healthy eating easier?
How has technology changed the way people shop for food?
What's your favourite app?
How much time do you spend on your phone each day?
Do you think people rely too much on technology?
Do you enjoy watching the news? Why or why not?
How often do you watch TV?
Is it okay to trust the things you see online and on TV news?
Do you think the contents of newspapers are reliable?
Where do you usually get your news from?
Do you follow international news or mainly local news?
Do you think social media is a reliable source of news?
Do you think it is ever okay to tell a lie?
Have you ever told a white lie to avoid hurting someone's feelings?
How do you feel when someone lies to you?
Are you a person who always tells the truth?
Do you think honesty is important in friendships?
Is it ever kind to tell a lie?
Were you taught to always tell the truth as a child?
Do you use any subscription services, such as streaming TV or music apps? Why or why not?
What was the first subscription you ever signed up for?
How do you usually pay for your subscriptions—monthly, yearly, or as a one-time payment?
Have you ever canceled a subscription? What was the reason?
Which streaming service do you use the most?
Do you think subscription services are good value for money?
Do you share subscriptions with family or friends?
Do you often ask others for advice?
Who do you usually ask when you need help?
Have you ever gotten lost while travelling?
Do you think good friends are necessary in your life?
What's the best piece of advice you've ever received?
Do you find it easy to give advice to others?
Do you prefer to figure things out yourself or ask for help?

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe your favourite city or a city you have visited that you like very much.
points: what its name is and where it is
and explain the major attractions in this city

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a piece of art or a drawing/painting that you like.
points: and explain why you like it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe an app or piece of technology that makes your life easier.
points: and explain why it makes your life easier

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a subscription service you use or have used.
points: how you found out about it
and explain how it has affected your life

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe your favourite shop.
points: and explain why you think it is a good shop

part2_cue_cards.topic: Talk about a time when you were not allowed to use your phone.
points: why you were not allowed to use it
and explain how you felt about it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time when technology helped you connect with someone.
points: why you needed to connect with them
and explain how it helped your relationship

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a house or apartment you would like to live in.
points: and explain why you would like to live there

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a change that could improve your local area.
points: and explain how it would improve the area

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a trip you took by public transport.
points: what form of transport you used
and explain what happened during the trip

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a close friend you have known for a long time.
points: and explain why your friendship has lasted

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a healthy dish you enjoy cooking.
points: how you learned to make it
and explain why you think it is healthy

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe an important environmental problem in your local area or country.
points: and explain what could be done to solve it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a person you know who lived alone abroad.
points: where and why they went abroad
how they adapted to living alone
and explain what you learned from their experience

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a person who is often in the news, and who you would like to meet.
points: why they are often in the news
and explain why you would like to meet them

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a piece of work you did for your job or your studies that you felt very satisfied with.
points: and explain why you felt satisfied with it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Talk about a group project that you worked on.
points: and explain how the project turned out

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a healthy habit you want to develop.
points: why you want to develop it
how you plan to develop it
and explain how it would benefit you

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a movie about wild animals that you enjoyed.
points: and explain why you enjoyed it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a food-related app or technology you find useful.
points: what app or technology it is
and explain why you find it helpful

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time when you received useful advice.
points: and explain why it was useful

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a successful businessman or a well-known person you know about.
points: and explain why people admire them

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe something cultural that you do not like.
points: and explain why you personally dislike it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time when you felt very proud of something a family member did.
points: and explain why it made you feel proud

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a car journey you remember well.
points: and explain why you remember it so well

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe something you do not like in your daily life.
points: and explain how you deal with it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a person who is good at learning and speaking new languages.
points: and explain why you think they are good at languages

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a boring place.
points: and explain why you found it boring

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time when you sent a message or an email to someone but received no reply for a long time.
points: how long you waited for a reply
and explain how you felt about it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a family member you spend a lot of time with.
points: what kind of person he/she is
and explain why you spend the most time with him/her

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe your experience of having your dream job.
points: what you do in this job
and explain how having your dream job has affected your life

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a school subject you enjoyed learning when you were younger.
points: what you learned in the class
and explain why you enjoyed it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a meal you enjoyed with friends.
points: and explain why you enjoyed that time

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time you looked for information from the internet.
points: what information you were looking for
which websites or apps you used
and explain whether you found what you needed

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a time when you had to deal with a difficult relationship in an educational setting.
points: and explain what you learned from the experience

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe an important conversation you had with someone.
points: and explain why it was important to you

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a helpful person.
points: what they did to help you
and explain why you consider them helpful

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a meaningful object you have kept since your childhood.
points: and explain why it is meaningful to you

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a restaurant where you paid attention to the nutritional information or ingredients of the food.
points: what kind of food it serves
why you paid attention to the ingredients
and explain how this affected your dining experience

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a person you have recently met but would like to know better.
points: and explain why you would like to know them better

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe an activity you would do when you are alone in your free time.
points: and explain why you enjoy doing it alone

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a sport that interests you but you have never tried.
points: what kinds of people usually play it
and say if you think you will ever try this sport, and why

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a book you have never read but would like to read.
points: how you found out about it
and explain why you would like to read it

part2_cue_cards.topic: Describe a workplace you have worked in or know about.
points: what kind of work is done there
and explain whether you think it is a good place to work

questions: Do you think technology has made communication between people easier or more difficult?
How has technology changed the way people shop for food?
Are there any disadvantages to using many subscription services at the same time?
In your opinion, will more things become 'subscription only' in the future? Why or why not?
Do you think technology makes life more complex? Should we simplify our lives by reducing our use of technology?
Do you think job satisfaction is more important than salary when choosing a job?
What skills do you think are needed to get a good job these days?
What's the biggest difference between white collar and blue collar jobs?
How important is work-life balance to you?
Do you think people should change jobs often, or stay in one job for a long time?
What can governments do to encourage people to protect the environment?
Do you think individuals can make a real difference to environmental problems, or is it mainly the responsibility of governments and large companies?
How can governments improve living quality in crowded cities?
What are the negative aspects of living in a crowded city?
Do you think the content in newspapers is reliable?
Is it necessary for people to keep up with international news?
What kinds of famous people are usually in the news in your country?
Do famous people have a responsibility to society?
How does media attention affect the private lives of famous people?
Do you think good friends are necessary in life?
Why is advice from experienced people valuable?
How do people decide whether to follow advice?
Do you often ask others for advice? Who do you usually ask?
Should schools teach children about healthy eating?
Is fast food always unhealthy?
What role does food play in different cultures?
Do you think modern society pays too much attention to food?
Do you think it is ever okay to tell a lie?
How does lying affect trust between people?
Are there cultural differences in attitudes towards lying?
How can people rebuild trust after a lie is discovered?
